title: Pappa al Pomodoro
subtitle: Tuscan bread and tomato soup
excerpt: One of the great Tuscan peasant dishes: stale bread torn into pieces and simmered with ripe tomatoes, garlic, and basil until everything collapses into a thick, porridge-like soup. Good olive oil turns it into something extraordinary.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pappa al pomodoro (pappa means pap or mush, a name that refers to its soft, thick texture) is a classic of the Tuscan cucina povera — the poor kitchen that made use of stale bread and abundant summer tomatoes. The dish requires stale, good-quality bread; fresh or soft bread will not give the right thick, cohesive texture. Tuscan unsalted bread (pane sciocco) is traditional; it soaks up liquid well and has a neutral flavour that lets the tomatoes and olive oil dominate. Tinned tomatoes can substitute for fresh in all but the height of summer, giving a consistent and perfectly acceptable result. The dish is served warm or at room temperature, never piping hot, as a thick, almost porridge-like soup.

content.text: The bread must be stale, at least 2 days old, and ideally from a country-style white loaf with a dense crumb. Fresh bread turns slimy rather than thickening properly. Use the best olive oil available: the olive oil is not just a garnish here, it is a central component. Serve at room temperature; leftovers improve overnight in the fridge and can be thinned with a little water or stock.

items.preparation: stale ciabatta or sourdough, crusts removed, torn into 2 cm pieces
2 tins whole plum, crushed by hand; or 1 kg very ripe fresh tomatoes, chopped
or water; plus extra if needed

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook very gently for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until it is soft and beginning to colour. Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down and the sauce is thick.

Add the bread pieces and stock. Stir everything together and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until the bread has completely absorbed the liquid and the soup is thick and porridge-like. Add a little more stock or water if it seems too stiff.

Season generously with salt and pepper. Stir in most of the basil. Leave to cool for 10 minutes before serving: pappa al pomodoro is best warm or at room temperature. Ladle into bowls, top with the remaining basil, and drizzle with a generous pour of extra-virgin olive oil.
